verdict.rationale: Braintrust's own docs say datasets can be built from production logs and that production data becomes versioned evaluation datasets. Those datasets then feed experiments run from code, the UI, the CLI, or CI/CD, with SDK Eval examples showing offline runs. missing for 10: detailed docs on the trace-to-dataset curation steps (e.g., selecting or filtering spans into a dataset), independent hands-on corroboration of the production-to-dataset-to-eval loop.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can curate datasets from production traces and run offline evaluations against them

citations.quote: Datasets are versioned collections of test cases that you use to run evaluations and track improvements over time. Build datasets from production logs, user feedback, manual curation, or generate them with Loop.
Production data seamlessly becomes evaluation datasets
Use a dataset for experiments or production traces for online scoring.

Experiments are the immutable, comparable record of your eval runs. Run them from code or in the UI, track progress over time, and integrate into CI/CD to catch regressions before they reach production.
Versioned: Every change is tracked, so experiments can pin to specific versions.
